summary: Sofalcone is a synthetic flavonoid derivative of sophoradin used in Japan as a gastroprotective (mucosal-protective) anti-ulcer agent for gastric ulcer, duodenal ulcer, and gastritis. It heals and protects the gastroduodenal mucosa primarily by increasing endogenous prostaglandin (PGE2) production and gastric mucus/bicarbonate secretion, scavenging reactive oxygen species, and inhibiting Helicobacter pylori colonization (it suppresses H. pylori chemotactic motility and, as an adjunct to standard eradication regimens, has increased cure rates in clinical studies). A typical adult dose is 100 mg orally three times daily. Sofalcone is NOT approved by the U.S. FDA; the information here is derived from Japanese drug monographs (PMDA-marketed product) and published clinical literature, not from a U.S. label. It is generally well tolerated, with mild gastrointestinal complaints being the most common adverse effects.

moa: Sofalcone is a synthetic flavonoid (isoprenyl chalcone/flavonoid) derived from sophoradin. Its gastroprotective and ulcer-healing actions are multifactorial: it stimulates synthesis and release of endogenous cytoprotective prostaglandins (notably PGE2), enhances gastric mucus and bicarbonate secretion, increases mucosal blood flow, and acts as an antioxidant by scavenging reactive oxygen species and reducing lipid peroxidation. It also has anti-Helicobacter pylori activity, including inhibition of H. pylori chemotactic motility, which impairs the organism's ability to colonize the gastric mucosa and contributes to improved eradication and ulcer-healing outcomes when combined with antibiotics.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to sofalcone or any component of the formulation

preg: Adequate human pregnancy data are lacking. Japanese product information advises use during pregnancy or possible pregnancy only when the expected benefit outweighs the potential risk. No U.S. pregnancy category is assigned because the drug is not FDA-approved.
lact: Data on excretion into human milk are insufficient. Use during breastfeeding only if clearly needed and after weighing benefit against potential risk to the infant.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is established; data in renal impairment are limited. Use with general caution and clinical monitoring.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is established; data in hepatic impairment are limited. Use with general caution and clinical monitoring.

interactions.alcohol: Avoid excessive alcohol, which aggravates gastric mucosal injury and peptic ulcer disease.

missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose and resume the regular schedule; do not double up.
overdose: No specific overdose syndrome or antidote is described in the available literature. In the event of overdose, provide supportive and symptomatic care and monitor the patient; contact a poison control center for guidance.
